MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Transform lives, every single day

Do you want a career that means more?

At Anglicare Sydney, we bring the strength, the support and the strategy to make it happen.

We're a well-respected not-for-profit that's been serving society's most vulnerable for over 170 years. Every purchase made in our Op Shops helps fund vital programs that support people experiencing hardship, while creating welcoming spaces where customers, volunteers and the local community feel valued, connected and supported.

As our Shop Assistant, you'll play an important role in delivering an exceptional customer experience while helping our Leura Op Shop continue to be a vibrant community hub. You'll work alongside a dedicated team of staff and volunteers to create an inviting retail environment where customers can discover quality pre-loved treasures and know their purchases are making a genuine difference.

Be welcomed into a compassionate, respectful and purpose-driven community where we don't just talk about values-we live them.

Your opportunity

As our Shop Assistant, you'll help create an enjoyable and memorable shopping experience by delivering outstanding customer service, maintaining attractive store presentation and supporting our incredible volunteer team.

You'll contribute to the smooth day-to-day operation of the shop while ensuring a safe, welcoming and inclusive environment for customers, volunteers and the wider Blue Mountains community.

With integrity and enthusiasm, you will:

- Deliver exceptional customer service and create a welcoming experience for every customer.

- Support, encourage and provide day-to-day guidance to volunteers while fostering a positive team culture.

- Assist with merchandising, stock presentation and maintaining an attractive, well-organised retail environment.

- Process sales, complete shop administration and ensure cash handling procedures are followed accurately.

- Maintain a safe, clean and organised workplace while actively promoting Anglicare's mission, vision and values.

What you'll bring

You are a friendly, energetic and customer-focused retail professional who enjoys connecting with people from all walks of life. You have a positive attitude, enjoy working collaboratively and are passionate about supporting your local community.

Whether you're helping a customer find the perfect item, merchandising new stock or supporting volunteers, you'll take pride in creating a welcoming shopping experience where . Compassion and Excellence.

You will also need:

- Previous retail or customer service experience.

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

- A genuine passion for helping people and serving your community.

- Ability to build positive relationships with customers, volunteers and colleagues.

- Current Working With Children Check (or willingness to obtain).

Ideally, you will also have:

- Experience in visual merchandising or retail presentation.

- Experience supporting or supervising volunteers.

- Cash handling and point-of-sale experience.

- A passion for sustainable retail, recycled fashion and giving pre-loved items a new purpose.

- Flexibility to assist with additional duties as required.

Why Anglicare?

We provide meaningful opportunities and choice, both for the individuals and communities we support and the dedicated people here who make it happen.

At Anglicare, you'll get the security, stability and opportunities that come with a strong, well-established organisation that's ready for the future. You'll belong to a community of kind, humble and respectful people of all faiths and backgrounds. You'll also be supported to gain new knowledge, deepen your experience and expertise, and shape a rewarding career.

- Pay less tax with salary packaging.

- Supportive and welcoming team environment.

- Ongoing learning and professional development opportunities.

- Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

- Fitness Passport.

- Exclusive discounts through our employee benefits program.

We're many services, with one purpose, to meet people where they are and walk with them.

At Anglicare, we believe everyone is Made for Connection-with God, with each other and with the places we call home. Every purchase made in our Op Shops helps fund services that support vulnerable children, families, older people and those experiencing hardship, making your work meaningful every single day.

Are you ready for a career that means more?

To apply for this role, please click the Apply button and submit your r sum together with a cover letter outlining your suitability for the role.

All applicants will receive a response.
 

Anglicare is as wonderfully diverse as the customers and communities we support. While we are guided by our Christian-based values, our team includes people of all faiths and backgrounds who share our commitment to serving others. Permanent Leadership Opportunity | Monday to Friday Role | Full Aviation Training Provided   Your new company     
 Gunggandji Aerospace is a proudly Aboriginal and veteran-owned Australian aviation and aerospace business delivering innovative solutions across the aviation sector. 
 In partnership with Toll Aviation, Gunggandji Aerospace is supporting the delivery of South Australia's State Police, Ambulance and Rescue Aviation Service (SPARAS), the critical aviation service responsible for police, ambulance and rescue missions across the state. 
 As part of the establishment of a new Aviation Operations Centre at Adelaide Airport, an exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Operations Supervisor to lead a team delivering an essential emergency aviation service to the South Australian community. 
 Gunggandji Aerospace is committed to creating a culturally safe, inclusive and supportive workplace and strongly encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. This position is open to all applicants. 
   Your new role     
 Reporting into the operational leadership team, you will lead a small team of Operations Controllers responsible for coordinating and monitoring emergency aviation missions across South Australia. 
 This role combines people leadership, workforce planning, stakeholder engagement and operational oversight. Working closely with Toll Aviation's SPARAS Aviation Operations Manager, you will support the successful day-to-day delivery of the service while ensuring a positive team culture, operational compliance and workforce wellbeing. 
 Primarily a Monday to Friday leadership position, with occasional participation in early and late operational shifts alongside your team. Full aviation and role-specific training provided. 
 
 
 Lead, mentor and develop a team of Operations Controllers and casual staff 
 
 
 Manage day-to-day team performance, coaching and employee wellbeing 
 
 
 Develop and maintain compliant workforce rosters, leave planning and fatigue management processes 
 
 
 Partner closely with Toll Aviation and operational stakeholders to ensure effective service delivery 
 
 
 Coordinate operational administration, reporting and workforce documentation 
 
 
 Monitor team compliance with operational procedures and safety requirements 
 
 
 Lead responses to operational disruptions and escalate matters as required 
 
 
 Foster a collaborative, high-performing and inclusive team culture 
 
 
   What you'll need to succeed     
 
 
 Demonstrated experience leading teams within an operational environment 
 
 
 Previous experience in aviation, emergency services, logistics, transport, operations centres or similar roster-based environments will be highly regarded 
 
 
 Strong people leadership and performance management capabilities 
 
 
 Experience managing rosters, workforce planning and employee-related matters 
 
 
 Understanding of award interpretation, workforce compliance or fatigue management principles, or the ability to quickly develop these skills 
 
 
 Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills 
 
 
 Strong computer literacy and reporting capabilities 
 
 
 The ability to remain calm, organised and solutions-focused in a dynamic environment 
 
 
 Willingness to work within a drug and alcohol-free workplace, including pre-employment and ongoing testing requirements 
 
 
 Eligibility to obtain: 
 
 
 National Police Check 
 
 
 Aviation Security Identification Card (ASIC) 
 
 
 WWCC 
 
 
 
 
 Availability to start from late August 2026 
 
 
 Ability to undergo initial training in Sydney 
 
 
   What you'll get in return     
 
 
 Attractive salary package of $90,000 - $100,000 plus superannuation 
 
 
 A leadership opportunity within a growing Aboriginal-owned aviation and aerospace business 
 
 
 Monday-Friday working arrangements with limited weekend requirements 
 
 
 Comprehensive onboarding and aviation industry training 
 
 
 Ongoing professional development and career growth 
 
 
 Supportive, inclusive and culturally safe workplace environment 
 
 
 The opportunity to play key role in supporting essential emergency aviation service that directly impacts communities across South Australia

About the Team 
 Our Fleet Maintenance team leads mechanical services and scheduled vehicle inspections to ensure all heavy, medium, and light commercial fleet assets are fit for purpose. Through a best-practice, full-lifecycle management approach, we maintain equipment deployed in complex environments, ensuring our operational capabilities consistently meet organisational objectives and strict regulatory guidelines. 
 About the Role 
 Reporting directly to the Workshop Supervisor, you will play a critical role in keeping our diverse fleet safe, compliant, and fully operational. You will be responsible for conducting high-quality repairs and scheduled maintenance on vehicle appliances, pumps, systems, and associated equipment. 
 A core focus of this role is ensuring that all fleet assets comply strictly with the National Heavy Vehicle Regulator (NHVR), Transport and Main Roads (TMR) legislative guidelines, the Queensland Transport Operations (Road Use Management - Road Rules) Regulations 2009, and the Transport Operations Act 1995. 
  Key Responsibilities:  
 
 
 Perform diagnostic, repair, and scheduled maintenance work on a diverse range of light, medium, and heavy commercial vehicles. 
 
 
 Service and repair vehicle appliances, high-pressure pumps, pneumatic, and hydraulic systems. 
 
 
 Ensure all maintenance meets NHVR and TMR legislative compliance standards. 
 
 
 Complete accurate and timely job sheets and data entry for all maintenance activities. 
 
 
 Champion a safe working environment by strictly adhering to all Workplace Health and Safety (WHS) policies and procedures. 
 
 
 What We Are Looking For 
 We are seeking a safety-focused and highly skilled Diesel Fitter who takes pride in producing quality work and maintaining meticulous compliance standards. 
  Mandatory Requirements:  
 
 
 Relevant Trade Qualification (Diesel Fitter / Heavy Commercial Vehicle Mechanic). 
 
 
 Ability to successfully pass a comprehensive pre-employment  Drug and Alcohol Test . 
 
 
 Ability to successfully pass a  Police Check . 
 
 
 Strong commitment to WHS practices and procedures. 
 
 
  Preferred Experience:  
 
 
 Demonstrated hands-on experience working with  High-Pressure Pumps, Pneumatics, and Hydraulics . 
 
 
 Previous experience working within NHVR and TMR compliance frameworks is highly regarded. 
 
 
 Why Join Us? 
 
 
  Monday to Friday Roster:  Enjoy your weekends and a genuine work-life balance. 
 
 
  Local Work:  Based locally in Townsville-be home every night. 
 
 
  Stability:  Long-term career security in a vital, compliance-driven fleet management environment. 
 
 
 How to Apply 
 If you have the skills, experience, and drive to keep our fleet moving safely, we want to hear from you. Please submit your up-to-date resume and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience. 

 At Randstad, we are passionate about providing equal employment opportunities and embracing diversity to the benefit of all. We actively encourage applications from any background. 
   
    Please  click here  to apply.

This is a permanent part-time role (6 hours per day) based in Anglicare Terraces, Paddigton.

Your opportunity 

At Anglicare, every moment matters - and as a Resident Services Coordinator, you'll be the welcoming face and trusted guide for our residents and their families. Like a dedicated concierge, you'll help create a personalised and seamless experience, ensuring every resident feels valued, supported and empowered to make the most of life in our community.

Think of this role as a Resident Concierge. You'll anticipate needs, personalise experiences, and connect residents with services that enrich their everyday lives. Through warmth, attention to detail and exceptional service, you'll help ensure every resident enjoys a welcoming, effortless and fulfilling experience from the moment they arrive.

As the first point of contact for residents, families, representatives and supporters, you'll coordinate our Higher Everyday Living services (Everyday Plus), helping residents discover and access experiences and services that enhance their independence, comfort and wellbeing. From guiding residents through service options and managing bookings to coordinating delivery, agreements, invoicing and reporting, you'll ensure every interaction is effortless, professional and centred on individual preferences.

Combining genuine hospitality with exceptional organisational skills, you'll become the go-to expert for Everyday Plus services, confidently supporting residents and colleagues while resolving enquiries with empathy and care. Working closely with site leaders, you'll continuously enhance the resident experience by identifying opportunities to improve services, drive innovation, and deliver outstanding outcomes.

This is more than a coordination role-it's an opportunity to create memorable experiences, build meaningful relationships, and make every resident feel truly at home.

What you'll bring 

Proven experience in customer service, hospitality, or residential aged care, with a strong resident-first mindset

Exceptional communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to engage confidently with residents, families, staff, and external stakeholders

Strong organisational and coordination skills, managing agreements, bookings, service delivery, feedback, invoicing, and reporting with care and precision

A proactive problem-solver, comfortable handling enquiries and complaints and escalating appropriately when required

Confidence using systems and databases, with the ability to act as a Subject Matter Expert for Higher Everyday Living IT systems

Commitment to delivering a high-quality resident experience, informed by feedback, consumer insights, and aged care trends

Understanding of compliance, privacy, and aged care standards, with a commitment to safety, continuous improvement, and best practice

Why Anglicare? 

For 170 years Anglicare has been serving those in need - providing care to older people and services to the vulnerable. Today we employ 6,000 staff and are blessed to serve alongside 1,500 volunteers. We provide meaningful opportunities and choice, both for the individuals and communities we support and the dedicated people here who make it happen. 

At Anglicare, you'll get the security, stability and opportunities that come with a strong, well-established organisation that's ready for the future. You will also be supported to gain new knowledge, deepen your experience and expertise, and shape a rewarding career. 

On top of that, here are just some of the tangible benefits you will enjoy in a career with us: 

Flexible work options to get the most out of work and life

The Grande Escape Resort in Margaret River have the following vacancies on offer:
- Hotel Manager

Hotel Manager

The manager will assume responsibility for overseeing day-to-day operations, ensuring guest satisfaction, directing staff, and maintaining profitability. The multifaceted responsibilities of this position demand business acumen, exceptional interpersonal skills, exceptional problem-solving skills and a genuine passion for guest service.

We are seeking a Hotel Manager to:
- Manage hotel services - accommodation and food and beverage.
- Oversee events and conferences.
- Manage corporate bookings and enquiries.
- Human resource management.
- Troubleshoot any issues arising in hotel operations.
- Liaise with contractors and suppliers.
- Supervise any maintenance work and renovations.
- Safeguard security and compliance, conducting inspections where necessary.
- Manage heads of departments or entire teams including supervision of ordering stock
- Drive forward sales strategies and oversee expenditure
- Handle financial responsibilities by ensuring high occupancy levels,
- Manage budgets and controlling expenditures.
- Track hotel revenues, setting sales targets and optimise profits.
- Analyse sales figures, reports and the different market segments and channels to define the best-suited pricing and distribution strategies.
- Maintain statistical and financial records.
- Monitor and motivate staff with constructive communication in a positive work environment and a shared vision of targets and career progression.

Skills and Qualifications:
- Diploma or degree in hospitality management or a related field.
- Two to five years of experience in a supervisory or management capacity within the hospitality industry.
- Exceptional leadership, interpersonal, and organisational abilities.
- Ability to lead people not just manage them.
- Proficiency in computer applications and hospitality management systems (RMS is preferable or similar).
- Willingness to work variable shifts, including weekends and holidays.
- Possess a police check or the ability to complete the check.

Hotel Service Manager

We are seeking a Hotel Service Manager to supervise daily operations and coordinate hotel service workers to ensure exceptional guest experiences. This will involve managing teams across front office, housekeeping, and concierge, balancing staff rosters, resolving grievances, and maintaining rigorous safety standards.

Key Responsibilities:
- Directs and delegates duties to housekeepers, maintenance and reception staff.
- Maintains attendance records, manages shift rosters, resolves staff grievances, and enforces safety regulations.
- Perform front office reception duties and ensure all hotel amenities meet strict brand and hygiene standards.
- Oversees the efficiency of hotel units and suggests operational improvements.

Qualifications & Requirements:
- Requires an AQF Certificate III/IV or Diploma in hospitality management.
- Requires two to three years of relevant on-the-job training or industry experience.
- Specialisation as a Front Office Manager with housekeeping experience; Food and beverage an advantage

Landscape Gardener

We are also seeking a Landscape Gardener to join our team, applicants must have at least 2-3 years' experience in a similar role.

Duties include:
- Preparing and maintaining seedbeds and growing sites
- Propagating and planting trees, bushes, hedges, flowers and bulbs
- Preparing lawn areas by spreading top soil and planting grass, and by laying instant turf
- Maintaining planted and grassed areas by weeding, trimming, fertilising, watering and mowing
- Ensuring the grounds are clean for guests
- Pruning trees and hedges, and installing plant support and protection devices
- Preparing plans and drawings, selecting materials and plants, and scheduling landscape construction
- Setting out and installing hardscape and softscape structures
- Constructing gravel and paved areas, walls, fences, pergolas, ponds, barbecues and garden furniture
- Examining trees to assess their condition and determine treatment
- Lopping limbs off trees and shaping branches using chain and handsaws
- Spraying and dusting plants and trees to control insects and disease, and felling diseased trees

Handyperson

In addition, we require a Handyperson to join our team full time as well.

You will be responsible for:
- General repairs around the property and rooms.
- Plumbing repairs including Unblocking sinks, fixing leaky taps, and replacing tap washers.
- Simple electrical repairs
- Painting and carpentry repairs to ensure the rooms and grounds are in good condition
- Outdoor maintenance such as clearing gutters, fixing fences, mowing lawns, and general yard upkeep.

Applicants must have:
- At least 1 year of experience in a similar role
- Proficiency in using hand and power tools.
- Basic working knowledge of carpentry, plumbing, and electrical systems
- Ability to perform manual labour, including lifting heavy objects and standing for long periods.
- Strong communication skills
- A valid driver's licence and relevant construction induction training (e.g., White Card in Australia)

A salary between $70,000 - $100,000 will be offered to the successful candidates.

If you are ready to take your career to the next level in a challenging, busy yet rewarding position, this may be the perfect opportunity for you.

At Anglicare, every moment matters - and as a Resident Services Coordinator, you'll be the welcoming face and trusted guide for our residents and their families. Like a dedicated concierge, you'll help create a personalised and seamless experience, ensuring every resident feels valued, supported and empowered to make the most of life in our community.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Unaccredited Trainee - Emergency Medicine, Royal North Shore Hospital

Employment Type: Various - Temporary Full Time, Temporary Part Time or Temporary Job Share
Remuneration: As per Public Hospital Medical Officers (State) Award
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: CAM30373

An exciting opportunity exists to join the dedicated Emergency Department at Royal North Shore Hospital. Be part of a multidisciplinary team delivering high-quality, patient-centred care within one of NSW's leading tertiary referral hospitals.

At Northern Sydney Local Health District (NSLHD), you'll enjoy a rewarding and flexible medical career with access to a diverse and complex case mix. Medical staff are actively involved in all aspects of patient care, working collaboratively across specialties to achieve the best outcomes for patients.

Whether you are looking to further develop your clinical skills, broaden your experience, or contribute to innovative models of care, NSLHD offers a supportive environment that encourages professional growth, education, and career development. Join a health service committed to excellence, innovation, and delivering exceptional care to the communities we serve.
 

Train at one of Australia's leading Emergency Departments!

The Emergency Medicine term at Royal North Shore Hospital (RNSH) offers an exceptional opportunity for junior doctors to develop expertise in the assessment and management of acute and complex presentations within a busy tertiary referral and major trauma centre.

As part of a highly skilled multidisciplinary team, trainees gain hands-on experience managing a broad range of medical, surgical, paediatric and trauma presentations, while working alongside experienced Emergency Physicians, specialty teams and critical care services. The term provides exposure to high-acuity patients, advanced resuscitation, trauma care and rapid clinical decision-making in a fast-paced environment.

RNSH is a major referral centre for Northern Sydney and New South Wales, providing specialist services including major trauma, neurosurgery, spinal cord injury, burns and critical care. This diverse case mix offers unparalleled learning opportunities and exposure to complex emergency presentations not commonly seen in smaller facilities.

The Emergency Medicine term is ideal for doctors seeking to develop strong acute care skills and provides an excellent foundation for future training in Emergency Medicine, Intensive Care Medicine, Anaesthetics and other acute care specialties. Trainees benefit from our strong culture of education, supervision and professional development, with access to formal teaching programs, simulation training and bedside learning designed to support both clinical growth and career progression.
 

Where you'll be working - Royal North Shore Hospital

Royal North Shore Hospital (RNSH) is a principal tertiary referral hospital within Northern Sydney Local Health District, delivering a comprehensive range of complex and highly specialised healthcare services to patients across Northern Sydney and New South Wales.

Unaccredited Trainee - Critical Care (Intensive Care Medicine & Anaesthesia) 

Temporary Full-Time

 

About the role 

The Manning Base Hospital Unaccredited Trainee Medical Officer programme offers interested and committed UATs interested in future rural practice the opportunity to develop knowledge, skills and gain experience in Critical Care, Anaesthesia and Acute Medicine. This program seeks to develop practitioners experienced with critical care skills, even though they may wish to subsequently train in different specialties, including Internal Medicine, Emergency Medicine, Intensive Care Medicine and Anaesthetics. 

Upon completion of the Critical Care UAT role doctors will be well prepared to apply for trainee positions or further training in Medicine, Intensive Care, Emergency Medicine or Anaesthetics and will also have acquired many transferable skills that will be useful in other training programs. This role is also highly relevant to those wanting to be an acute generalist (e.g. ACCRM RACGP-Rural). 

 

A structured programme with rotations in Anaesthesia (minimum of 2 terms) and other relevant Critical Care specialties (e.g. ED - Acute Medicine - General Medicine - Intensive Care) within a 12 month period. 

 

Medical Officers must be a PGY4 at the commencement of this role to be eligible. 

 

Participation in relief - nights are expected on an equitable basis. 

The applicant must have a commitment to rural practice and rural communities. 

For further details please refer to the Position Description. 

An Elist will be created for future appointments. 

 

Where you'll be working 

Taree's, town name comes from the Aboriginal word Djarii, meaning Figtree. Taree is situated on the banks of the Manning River in the heart of the beautiful Manning Valley, Biripi Country. A spectacular meeting point of coastal beauty and hinterland wonder, the Manning Valley is a gem on the NSW North Coast. Cruise the beautiful river, swim at stunning beaches and find bushwalks, waterfalls and lookouts along the way. 

Manning Hospital consists of 180 beds and, within, provides an excellent range of other specialist inpatient services including Emergency Medicine, General Medicine, Paediatrics, General Surgery, Orthopaedics, Intensive Care, Psychiatry, Renal, Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Anaesthesia, Rehabilitation Services, Urology and Oncology Services to the local communities of Taree, Forster, Tuncurry, Greater Taree and Gloucester local government areas. 

Manning Base Hospital treats approximately 25,000 inpatients, 33,000 Emergency Department patients and 90,700 outpatients each year. 

With a population of over 90,300 and with the median age of 52 years old the Lower Mid North Coast Sector is projected to have the highest growth in the group age of 85 years and over. 

Skills and Experience should be in line with but not limited to the attached Position Description. 

What we can offer you 

Hunter New England Local Health District (HNELHD) is a great place to expand your career and grow your skills and knowledge. As a recognised leader in the healthcare industry we provide a range of public health services to the Hunter New England and Lower Mid North Coast sector. Being the largest employer in the region we can offer salary packaging options, educational opportunities and support from a broad network of health professionals. With CORE Values of Collaboration, Openness, Respect and Empowerment your professional life is provided every opportunity to succeed and develop in your Medical Career. 

Working with HNE Health gives you access to a great range of benefits: 

Sustainable Healthcare: Together towards zero

Positions are available at St Vincent's Hospital Sydney and comprises rotations in Intensive Care, Anaesthetics, Emergency Medicine and General Medicine. The Senior Resident Medical Officer (SRMO) is responsible for co-ordinating and documenting the admission, management and discharge planning of patients within the Unit; the day-to-day assessment and management of the patients, maintaining high levels of communication with patients and family regarding the nature of their condition and its treatment; communicating and co-ordinating care with the team; arranging consultation with other staff when appropriate; support and education for interns and junior residents and arranging discharge and liaising with local medicalofficers and other community based care modalities in order to ensure the provision of optimal patient care within St Vincent's Health Network. 

It is anticipated that SRMOs will complete a research or quality assurance project related to critical care in the year. 

What you'll be doing
This role offers candidates an opportunity to enhance their knowledge, skills and experience in Anaesthesia, Intensive Care Medicine, Emergency Medicine and General Medicine. This role is an opportunity to develop in ANZCA roles in practice: medical expert, communicator, collaborator, leader and manager, health advocate, scholar, and professional. 

The SRMO Anaesthesia positions are suitable for applicants wishing to obtain further general Anaesthetics and Critical Care experience in preparation for a critical care career pathway. 
 

Where you'll be working

Where you'll be working

Cruise the beautiful river, swim at stunning beaches and find bushwalks, waterfalls and lookouts along the way. 

Manning Hospital consists of 180 beds and, within, provides an excellent range of other specialist inpatient services including Emergency Medicine, General Medicine, Paediatrics, General Surgery, Orthopaedics, Intensive Care, Psychiatry, Renal, Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Anaesthesia, Rehabilitation Services, Urology and Oncology Services to the local communities of Taree, Forster, Tuncurry, Greater Taree and Gloucester local government areas. 

Manning Base Hospital treats approximately 25,000 inpatients, 33,000 Emergency Department patients and 90,700 outpatients each year. 

With a population of over 90,300 and with the median age of 52 years old the Lower Mid North Coast Sector is projected to have the highest growth in the group age of 85 years and over. 

Skills and Experience should be in line with but not limited to the attached Position Description. 

What we can offer you 

Hunter New England Local Health District (HNELHD) is a great place to expand your career and grow your skills and knowledge. As a recognised leader in the healthcare industry we provide a range of public health services to the Hunter New England and Lower Mid North Coast sector. Being the largest employer in the region we can offer salary packaging options, educational opportunities and support from a broad network of health professionals. With CORE Values of Collaboration, Openness, Respect and Empowerment your professional life is provided every opportunity to succeed and develop in your Medical Career. 

Working with HNE Health gives you access to a great range of benefits: 

Sustainable Healthcare: Together towards zero 

ADO's each month (for full time employees) 

Access to the UONDRH, in addition conjoint lecturer opportunities 

Teaching and mentoring programs 

Long service leave and paid Maternity leave

Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for staff and family members 

Opportunity to work and collaborate with a range of non-clinical and clinical professionals 

Access to the highly sought after Work Place Based Assessment Program (WBA)
